gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured energy balance for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus. StorageReview (Dylan Dougherty, Jan 2, 2025) drew 910 Wh out of the 1,024 Wh pack (88.9%) and needed 1,180 Wh in to refill it from 0 to 100% (86.8%). At the full 1,000 W of solar through its two ports, the input side works out to about 71 minutes, which matches EcoFlow's 70-minute claim. Separately, The Solar Lab reports getting 'really close to' 1,000 W with both 500 W ports in use.
standout_why: I checked six pages. Volt & Valley's combo page (cited) says the DELTA 3 Plus has 'two MPPT inputs of 500W each' but reports no measured figures and uses its own 75%/85% assumptions. Amphourly's mid-size page (updated 2026-10-24) has specs and calculated runtimes only. Off Grid Benchmark's DELTA 3 Plus review says 'I have not tested this unit'. Popular Science's Elite 100 V2 review has no figures, only 'roughly accurate' for the 70-minute claim. Our own current page already cites The Solar Lab's near-1,000 W two-port reading but has no measured usable Wh or refill energy. No ChatGPT result has StorageReview's 910 Wh out / 1,180 Wh in, or Techreviewer.de's 946 Wh at 500 W for the Elite 100 V2. thiswatt.com and nymag.com (Strategist, cited) would not open, so I could not check them.
decides: This confirms the DELTA 3 Plus as the pick. It is the only candidate where a named tester actually drew close to 1,000 W through two inputs (The Solar Lab, both 500 W ports, Serious 415 W bifacial panels). Its measured efficiency (88.9% out, 86.8% in, StorageReview) means the 70-minute solar claim holds only if the full 1,000 W keeps coming in. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 tested similarly well on capacity (946 Wh at a 500 W load, Techreviewer.de). But it has one DC input (12–60 V, 20 A), so it fails the 'two inputs' requirement. No named reviewer I could open logged its solar watts. It also idles at about 16 W with the inverter on (The Solar Lab), and its AC charging drops to about 500 W below 20% charge.
